config.title: break-inside and pagination

intro.title: break-inside and pagination
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple multi-column article layout that demonstrates how to control where content breaks across pages or columns. You will learn the core CSS concept of the 'break-inside' property to prevent unwanted splits in elements like images or paragraphs. The main technologies involved are CSS properties for pagination and column layout, specifically 'break-inside' and 'column-count'. By the end, you'll understand how to use these properties to create cleaner, more readable printed or multi-column web content.
intro.usecase: The break-inside property is essential for creating professional print-ready documents and multi-column layouts that maintain readability across page breaks. Developers use it in dashboard reporting tools to prevent charts and data tables from being awkwardly split between printed pages. E-commerce platforms apply break-inside to product catalogs and invoices, ensuring product descriptions and pricing tables stay intact when customers print receipts. Content management systems also utilize this property for articles and documentation, keeping code examples and images together in multi-column magazine-style layouts.

objectives: Apply the break-inside property to prevent content from splitting across page or column boundaries.
Configure CSS pagination rules to control how content flows in print media.
Construct a multi-column layout and implement break control within specific elements.
Manipulate page breaks before and after elements using the break-before and break-after properties.
Integrate break-inside with other CSS properties to maintain visual integrity in paginated content.
Initialize a print stylesheet that applies pagination controls to a structured HTML document.
Render a document preview that demonstrates controlled breaks across pages or columns.

steps.title: Add CSS print media query for pagination
steps.instruction: Inside the <style> tags in your HTML, add a @media print query to create a print-specific styles section.
steps.hint: Use @media print { } to define styles that will only apply when printing the document.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Pagination Demo</title>
  <style>
    /* CSS will be added in later steps */
    @media print {
      /* Add print styles here */
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <!-- Add your container and sections here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: A @media print query is added inside the <style> tags, ready for print-specific CSS rules.
successCriteria: The code contains a valid @media print query inside the <style> tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added @media print { } inside the <style> tags.
steps.feedbackWrong: The print media query is missing. Add @media print { } inside the <style> tags.

steps.expectedOutcome: The @page rule is added inside the print media query, defining A4 page size with 2cm margins.
successCriteria: The @page rule with size: A4 and margin: 2cm is present inside the @media print block.

steps.title: Use orphans and widows for line control
steps.instruction: Inside the print media query, add CSS rules for the .content class to set orphans: 3 and widows: 3.
steps.hint: The orphans property sets the minimum number of lines that must be left at the bottom of a page. The widows property sets the minimum number of lines that must appear at the top of a page. Setting both to 3 helps prevent single lines from appearing alone on pages.
